title: Add NCCL all-reduce smoke test to post-provision validation (fabric sanity)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Context
We’re seeing a non-trivial class of “looks fine until real workload” failures during Dedicated pool expansions: nodes successfully join the cluster, GPU is visible, driver parity checks pass, but collective performance/communication is broken or unstable (miswired fabric, bad NIC, incorrect interface selection, MTU mismatch, etc.). These then show up as runtime errors or degraded throughput after the node is added to serving pools.

Goal
Add a lightweight NCCL all-reduce smoke test to the post-provision validation gates so we catch fabric issues before a node is marked Ready and before it can join serving pools.

Scope
- Implement a post-provision validation step: NCCL all-reduce smoke test.
- Tune timeouts and retries so the test is actionable and doesn’t become a high-flake gate.
- Emit structured validation artifacts (result + stderr excerpt + metrics) to Fleet Readiness Service.
- Provide safe defaults for early rollout (us-east / A100), with feature flagging and thresholds configurable by GPU type.

Non-goals
- Full perf benchmarking or long-running soak tests.
- Automatically repairing fabric issues (we’ll quarantine + reimage/escalate per runbook).

Proposed design
Validation step name
- validation_step = "nccl_allreduce_smoke"

Implementation approach
- Run inside the node validation agent (DaemonSet) after kubelet join + after GPU health + driver parity validations pass.
- Use a container image that includes nccl-tests (or a minimal binary) with pinned versions matching the golden image driver/CUDA/NCCL matrix.
- Execute a short all-reduce across all GPUs on the node (intra-node) and (where applicable) a small cross-node ring test against a small peer set when the pool is being expanded in batches.
  - Phase 1 (this ticket): intra-node only (fast, low dependency).
  - Phase 2 (follow-up if needed): optional cross-node peer test (more signal for fabric but more coordination).

Command (intra-node)
- Prefer: /opt/nccl-tests/all_reduce_perf
- Example:
  - all_reduce_perf -b 8M -e 64M -f 2 -g <num_gpus> -n 20
- Capture:
  - exit code
  - parsed busbw/algbw summary
  - wall time
  - stderr tail (last 100 lines) for actionable Xid/NCCL error hints

Pass/fail criteria (initial)
- Hard fail on any non-zero exit code or NCCL error signatures.
- Bandwidth threshold gate (soft -> hard by rollout stage):
  - Candidate stage: record bandwidth but do not quarantine solely on bandwidth unless < 50% baseline
  - Stable stage: quarantine if < 70% baseline for the GPU type
- Baselines:
  - A100 (8x) us-east: baseline recorded from known-good nodes; store per GPU SKU baseline in config.

Timeouts / retries / flake mitigation
- Warm-up run: 1 short warm-up iteration to avoid first-run overhead being mistaken as failure.
- Timeout: 3 minutes (per attempt) for intra-node test.
- Retry policy:
  - retry up to 1 time if the error matches a known transient bucket (e.g., "unhandled system error" without Xid, or container runtime hiccup).
  - do NOT retry on deterministic errors (interface selection failures, Xid/ECC, explicit NCCL WARN/ERROR with stack).
- CPU/GPU contention:
  - pin test to run only when node is not scheduled for inference workloads (still in Validating).
  - set low process priority and conservative CUDA device usage.

Telemetry
- Emit to readiness service:
  - validation_result: pass/fail/quarantined
  - duration_ms
  - attempts
  - parsed_algbw_gbps, parsed_busbw_gbps
  - failure_reason_code (enum-ish string)
  - logs_uri (pointer to bundled logs)
- Metrics:
  - provision_validation_step_latency_ms{step="nccl_allreduce_smoke", gpu_type, region}
  - provision_validation_step_success_total{step="nccl_allreduce_smoke", gpu_type, region}
  - provision_validation_step_failure_total{step="nccl_allreduce_smoke", reason, gpu_type, region}

Rollout plan
- Start behind feature flag: enable_nccl_smoke_validation
- Initial enablement: us-east + A100 Dedicated pools only (aligned with ENG-4829 rollout).
- Ramp:
  1) Observe-only (record results, do not quarantine on bandwidth) for 48 hours
  2) Quarantine on hard failures + severe perf (<50% baseline)
  3) Quarantine on hard failures + perf (<70% baseline) after flake rate is acceptable

Acceptance criteria
- [x] NCCL smoke test runs as part of post-provision validation for enabled pools.
- [x] Failure reasons are actionable in readiness UI/log artifacts (not just “NCCL failed”).
- [x] End-to-end time-to-ready impact: +<5 minutes at P95 for enabled pools.
- [x] Flake rate: <1% “passes on retry” once tuned (measured over at least 200 nodes).
- [x] SRE sign-off on alerting: no paging on initial rollout; ticket-only until thresholds stabilize.

Links / references
- Fleet readiness state machine: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-017-provision-to-ready-readiness-state-machine.json
- Validation agent deployment: sources/github/redwood-helm-charts/pr-244-add-node-validation-agent-daemonset.json
- Metrics step breakdown PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-18441-emit-provision-to-ready-metrics-step-breakdown.json
- Flake follow-ups: ENG-4830

Open questions
- Do we need cross-node testing in phase 1 for H100 clusters (stronger signal for fabric)?
- Should bandwidth thresholds differ by topology (PCIe vs SXM) and by NIC/fabric type?

Owner
- Gabe Wilson (implementation)
- Nina Petrova (threshold sanity + topology guidance)
- Aisha Bello (dashboarding / alert tuning guidance)
comments: 2025-10-04 (Nina Petrova): Intra-node all-reduce is a good first gate. It will catch “bad GPU/NVLink topology” and some driver/runtime issues, but it won’t catch ToR/IB issues. I’m ok shipping intra-node first; add optional cross-node peer test later once orchestration is stable.

2025-10-06 (Aisha Bello): Please be careful with metric cardinality. No per-node IDs or hostnames in tags. Use gpu_type + region + pool_type + step + reason only. Also recommend ticket-only alerts initially; paging will be noisy during rollout.

2025-10-08 (Gabe Wilson): Prototype running nccl-tests inside validation agent. Noted that first run is slower; adding warm-up. Also saw occasional failure when containerd pulls image slowly; marking that retry-eligible.

2025-10-10 (Rafael Mendes): For retry policy, avoid retrying actual NCCL errors that are likely deterministic. Recommend pattern match: retry only on infra/container startup or transient “unhandled system error” without Xid. Everything else -> quarantine (or fail validation) to keep Ready signal meaningful.

2025-10-13 (Keiko Yamamoto): Make thresholds config-driven by gpu_type and allow per-region overrides (we’ve seen MTU diffs). Also: keep runtime under 3–4 minutes per node or we’ll blow P95 time-to-ready.

2025-10-16 (Gabe Wilson): Tuning update: using -b 8M -e 64M -f 2 -n 20 keeps duration ~70–110s on A100 8x. Added 180s timeout per attempt, 1 retry only for container-startup/pull failures. Recording busbw/algbw for later analysis.
2025-10-18 (Vanessa Ortiz): Approved for staged rollout in us-east A100 only (observe-only for first 48h; quarantine on hard failures immediately). Please link runbook section once docs PR lands.

2025-10-22 (Gabe Wilson): Shipped and enabled in us-east A100 (observe-only bandwidth gate). Flake rate from first 230 nodes: 0.8% retry-pass; hard failures 2 nodes (one consistent NCCL error, one GPU Xid) quarantined and escalated. Creating follow-up for cross-node peer mode experiment under separate flag.
